title: The Retake Slide
question: 'If students may retake tests, soon degrees mean nothing, employers trust nothing, and education collapses.' No mechanism links these steps. Which fallacy is this?
correctExplanation: Slippery slope — a cascade asserted without mechanisms: retakes to collapse with no gears shown. Horror substitutes for linkage.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is slippery slope. No straw man (no position distorted), no personal attack, no tradition invoked — just an unevidenced slide from retakes to ruin. Mechanisms missing is the diagnosis.
lessonContent:
Cascades need gears, never just horror.
Unevidenced slides trade dread for proof.
Retakes-to-ruin skips every linkage.
Demand mechanisms per step always.
Share this: demand one slope's gears today.

title: The Creeping Mandate
question: Emergency surveillance powers, renewed yearly with documented widening scope each cycle, keep expanding. Critics call the expansion inevitable. What makes this slope claim serious?
choices: A documented mechanism at each step
correctAnswer: A documented mechanism at each step
correctExplanation: Documented mechanisms — renewal procedures plus recorded widening give each step gears and history. Serious slopes show receipts.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is a documented mechanism at each step. Necessity proofs, moods, and coincidences miss it: yearly renewals plus scope logs make expansion traceable. Evidence per step separates warnings from panics.
lessonContent:
Receipts separate warnings from panics.
Renewal logs trace expansion stepwise.
Mechanisms plus history make slopes serious.
Documented gears beat dreaded visions.
Share this: check one mandate's scope log.

title: The Gateway Test
question: 'Soft-drug use leads to hard-drug ruin' is invoked to ban the former. As logic rather than policy, what would validate this slope?
correctExplanation: Evidence per transition — correlation plus plausible stepping-stones, tested stepwise. Slopes stand on transition data, never on dread.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is evidence for each transition. Disapproval, confessions, and inevitability skip the work: each link needs its own rate and mechanism. Gateway claims are empirical hypotheses wearing logical clothes.
lessonContent:
Gateways are hypotheses, never axioms.
Each link needs rates and mechanisms.
Dread dresses as logic too easily.
Transition data validates slope talk.
Share this: demand one gateway's rates.

title: The Widening Lens
question: Protest surveillance authorized for terrorism cases appears years later in drug and immigration cases, with memos showing deliberate repurposing. What kind of slope is this?
correctExplanation: A precedent-backed cascade — memos plus mission drift document each widening. Precedent is the grease slopes slide on.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is a precedent-backed cascade. Panic, straw, and insult mislabel it: repurposing memos supply mechanism and history together. Documented drift is the genuine article.
lessonContent:
Memos supply mechanisms plus history.
Drift documented is drift demonstrated.
Precedent greases every genuine slope.
Repurposing leaves paper trails always.
Share this: follow one paper trail.

title: The Euthanasia Evidence
question: Debates invoke inevitable expansion from assisted dying to involuntary killing. Set passions aside: what should decide whether this slope is real?
correctExplanation: Step-by-step data — jurisdictional records showing whether each feared expansion occurred. Horror stories illustrate; registries decide.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is step-by-step data, not horror stories. Pulpits, ancients, and anecdotes skip the method: compare regimes with and without safeguards over decades. Slopes are settled by ledgers.
lessonContent:
Registries decide what stories illustrate.
Jurisdictions compared test slope claims.
Safeguards either hold or fail measurably.
Ledgers settle slopes; anecdotes start them.
Share this: read one registry, not one story.

title: The Domino Claim
question: 'If one nation falls to communism, neighbors will topple in sequence' — the Vietnam-era domino theory. Logically, what status does this claim hold?
choices: A historical slope claim needing evidence
correctAnswer: A historical slope claim needing evidence
correctExplanation: A slope claim needing evidence — dominoes need transmission mechanisms (funding, insurgents, borders), not metaphors. History grades such claims case by case.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is a historical slope claim needing evidence. Laws, theorems, and insults misclassify it: game pieces don't capture insurgency logistics. Some dominoes fell, others stood — mechanisms decided.
lessonContent:
Metaphors never substitute for mechanisms.
Transmission needs funders and foot soldiers.
History grades slope claims case by case.
Game pieces mislead strategists badly.
Share this: test one domino theory.

title: The Ban Horizon
question: 'Ban one book and censors will advance title by title.' When does this warning rise above fallacy?
correctExplanation: Motive plus precedent — stated censor goals plus prior expansions supply mechanism and history. Warnings with both earn attention.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is motive plus precedent for expansion. Volume, complaints, and sales miss it: censors announcing lists plus following them before makes slopes credible. Goals stated plus goals pursued equals gears.
lessonContent:
Stated goals plus pursued lists equal gears.
Censors telegraph slopes in manifestos.
Precedent converts warnings into forecasts.
Motive plus history beats volume always.
Share this: read one censor's manifesto.

title: The Tipping Cascade
question: Warming melts permafrost, releasing methane, driving more warming — a self-reinforcing loop climate scientists quantify. What makes this slope legitimate?
choices: A physical cascade with measured feedbacks
correctAnswer: A physical cascade with measured feedbacks
correctExplanation: A measured physical cascade — feedback gains quantified in watts per square meter, not rhetoric. Physics supplies gears skepticism cannot vote down.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is a physical cascade with measured feedbacks. Consensus, repetition, and optimism miss it: methane fluxes and albedo losses are metered. Legitimate slopes carry instruments.
lessonContent:
Feedbacks metered beat rhetoric always.
Watts per square meter settle cascades.
Physics supplies gears votes cannot remove.
Legitimate slopes carry instruments.
Share this: meter one feedback loop.

title: The Resistance Slope
question: Each antibiotic course slightly raises population resistance; widespread use breeds untreatable strains. Doctors call this a genuine slope. Why does it qualify?
correctExplanation: A genuine slope — selection pressure mechanizes every step: use kills susceptibles, survivors inherit. Evolution guarantees the slide.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is a genuine use-breeds-resistance slope. Pitches, coincidences, and accidents miss it: Darwinian selection is the documented gear. Slopes with evolution behind them are timetables, not speculations.
lessonContent:
Selection mechanizes every step here.
Survivors inherit what prescriptions select.
Evolution guarantees slides it touches.
Timetables differ from speculations.
Share this: finish one full course.

title: The Doom Chain
question: 'AI research leads to superintelligence leads to extinction' — a three-link chain to doom. As presented without numbers, what is missing?
correctExplanation: Missing probabilities — chains multiply uncertainties: even likely-seeming links compound to long shots. Unquantified doom is mood, not forecast.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is missing probabilities at each link. Jargon, optimism, and celebrities miss it: three 50% links yield 12.5%, not near-certainty. Chains need numbers or they are narratives.
lessonContent:
Chains multiply uncertainties brutally.
Unquantified doom is mood, not forecast.
Links need numbers, never just names.
Narratives pose as forecasts daily.
Share this: price one chain's links.

title: The Slope Standard
question: Philosophers ask when slope arguments are legitimate rather than fallacious. What is the standing test?
correctExplanation: Evidence per step — likelihood times mechanism at each link. Tests beat tastes in slope evaluation.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is evidence for every step's likelihood. Delivery, pedigree, and brevity miss it: legitimacy is earned link by link with data. Standards apply to warnings and reassurances alike.
lessonContent:
Legitimacy is earned link by link.
Likelihood times mechanism: the formula.
Standards bind warnings and reassurances.
Tests beat tastes in evaluations.
Share this: apply the standard once.

title: The Loyalty Ultimatum
question: 'You're either with us or against us' — no neutral ground admitted in a national crisis. Which fallacy structures this demand?
correctExplanation: False dilemma — neutrality, criticism-with-loyalty, and indifference are real positions the ultimatum erases. Two doors posted where hallways exist.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is false dilemma. No slope slides, no tradition appeals, no straw stuffed: options are amputated, not argued. Crises love binaries; reality keeps hallways.
lessonContent:
Ultimatums amputate real hallways.
Neutrality exists though unposted.
Binaries comfort; hallways describe.
Crises manufacture false pairs routinely.
Share this: walk one unposted hallway.

title: The Market Binary
question: 'Either totally free markets or total state control — pick one.' Debates staged this way hide functioning alternatives. What do they omit?
correctExplanation: Mixed economies — every prosperous nation blends markets with states. Binaries hide the actual address everyone lives at.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is mixed economies as excluded middle. Tickers, coins, and celebrities miss it: the omitted middle houses the whole developed world. Extremes debate; mixtures govern.
lessonContent:
Mixtures govern where extremes debate.
Omitted middles house whole nations.
Blends work; purities preach.
Binaries hide lived addresses.
Share this: inhabit one middle consciously.

title: The Classroom Binary
question: 'Either iron discipline or total chaos — strictness is the only alternative to anarchy in schools.' What lies between?
correctExplanation: Authoritative structure — warm demandingness: firm boundaries plus real regard. Research favors the middle the slogan deletes.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is authoritative structure between extremes. Days, volumes, and uniforms miss it: demanding plus responsive outperforms both drill and drift. Middles parent better than poles.
lessonContent:
Demanding plus responsive beats both poles.
Warmth with boundaries parents best.
Deleted middles outperform posted extremes.
Authoritative differs from authoritarian.
Share this: hold one warm boundary.

title: The Faith Binary
question: 'Choose science or religion — reason and faith cannot coexist.' History overflows with counterexamples. What does the ultimatum erase?
correctExplanation: Compatibilist middles — Gould's magisteria, synthesis theologies, compartmentalized labs. Millennia of coexistence refute the forced choice.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is compatibilist middle positions. Equipment, books, and debates miss it: coexistence is the historical norm, conflict the recent invention. Ultimatums rewrite crowded middles as empty.
lessonContent:
Coexistence is the historical norm.
Conflict narratives invent recent wars.
Crowded middles refute forced choices.
Magisteria can share one mind.
Share this: inhabit one crowded middle.

title: The Nature Binary
question: 'Behavior is either all genes or all upbringing.' Modern biology answers differently. What replaces the duel?
correctExplanation: Gene-environment interaction — heritability varies by context; environments switch genes. The duel dissolves into interplay.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is gene-environment interaction. Scans, sequencers, and twins miss it as answers: tools confirm interplay, never victors. Nature loads dice environments roll.
lessonContent:
Dice loaded, then rolled by contexts.
Interplay dissolves nature-nurture duels.
Heritability varies; interaction persists.
Contexts switch genes routinely.
Share this: retire one duel framing.

title: The Highway Demand
question: 'My way or the highway' — negotiations framed as accept-or-walk. Skilled mediators reject the frame itself. What do they introduce?
correctExplanation: Integrative options — trades across differently-valued issues create joint gains. Highways multiply when interests differ.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is integrative win-win options. Volume, asphalt, and clocks miss it: differing valuations enable trades ultimatums hide. Reject frames before picking doors.
lessonContent:
Differing valuations enable joint gains.
Frames rejected beat doors picked.
Highways multiply with creativity.
Interests differ; use the difference.
Share this: invent one third door.

title: The Patriot Trap
question: 'Love it or leave it' — dissent branded disloyalty, reform equated with rejection. What democratic option does this erase?
correctExplanation: Loyal dissent — loving criticism that stays and repairs. Democracies need loyal opposition, not exit ramps.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is loyal dissent and reform. Emigration, anthems, and quiet miss it: patriotism includes repair crews, not just cheerleaders. Staying critics love countries enough to fix them.
lessonContent:
Repair crews love countries deeply.
Staying critics fix what leavers abandon.
Dissent can be loyalty's highest form.
Cheerleaders never repaired anything.
Share this: dissent loyally once.

title: The Growth Binary
question: 'Either endless growth or a livable planet — choose.' Degrowth and green-growth camps both say the frame cheats. What does the dilemma omit?
correctExplanation: The decoupling debate — whether growth can shed material throughput divides serious camps. Omission, not error, is the fallacy.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is the omitted decoupling debate. Parades, arithmetic, and printing miss it: both rival camps live in the excluded middle. Binaries hide debates, never settle them.
lessonContent:
Rival camps can share one excluded middle.
Binaries hide debates instead of settling.
Omission, not error, defines false dilemmas.
Decoupling decides what binaries obscure.
Share this: inhabit one omitted debate.

title: The Drum Binary
question: 'Bombs or talks — hawks versus doves, no middle ground.' Statecraft textbooks operate elsewhere. What functions between?
correctExplanation: Diplomacy backed by deterrence — coercive bargaining blends both poles. Statecraft lives in compounds, not elements.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is diplomacy backed by deterrence. Drums, pillows, and jets miss it: threats enable talks, talks channel threats. Middles govern; poles perform.
lessonContent:
Compounds govern where elements perform.
Threats enable talks they seem to oppose.
Middles blend what poles pretend excludes.
Statecraft mixes; punditry separates.
Share this: blend one hawk with one dove.

title: The Grade Binary
question: 'Either grades motivate or nobody learns anything.' Mastery-based classrooms falsify this daily. What replaces the binary?
correctExplanation: Mastery-based systems — competence, autonomy, and purpose motivate without rank. Learning thrives ungraded.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is mastery-based intrinsic systems. Cards, packs, and rooms miss it: self-determination theory relocates motivation inside learners. Grades rent attention; mastery owns it.
lessonContent:
Motivation relocates inside learners.
Competence, autonomy, purpose: the triad.
Rented attention differs from owned mastery.
Grades motivate ranking, rarely learning.
Share this: master one thing ungraded.

title: The Censor Binary
question: 'Either censor misinformation or drown in lies.' Researchers list further instruments. What else belongs in the toolkit?
correctExplanation: Counterspeech, friction, and literacy — reply, slow, and educate alongside any removal. Toolkits beat binaries in information policy.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is counterspeech, friction, and literacy. Megaphones, takedowns, and blindfolds miss the repertoire: more speech, careful design, and skilled readers. Binaries shrink toolkits to hammers.
lessonContent:
Repertoires beat binaries in policy.
Reply, slow, educate: the trio.
Hammers see nails; toolkits see systems.
Literacy is infrastructure, not luxury.
Share this: counterspeak once today.

title: The Security Binary
question: 'Privacy or security — pick one,' surveillance debates insist. Oversight regimes claim both are kept. What squares the circle?
correctExplanation: Oversight with targeted powers — judges, minimization, and audits keep tools sharp and scoped. Design dissolves false trades.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is oversight with targeted powers. Walls, chips, and sirens miss it: scope plus supervision squares liberty with safety. Trades accepted blindly are rarely necessary.
lessonContent:
Design dissolves false trades routinely.
Scope plus supervision squares circles.
Blind trades are rarely necessary.
Liberty and safety share engineers.
Share this: demand one oversight mechanism.

title: The Owl Binary
question: 'Jobs or spotted owls — loggers or birds.' The Pacific Northwest fight was framed so. What compromise actually existed?
correctExplanation: Transition support plus selective harvest — retraining funds plus uneven-aged logging kept workers and owls. Middles existed unadvertised.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is transition support plus selective harvest. Chainsaws, speed, and quiet miss it: the Northwest Plan funded both paychecks and habitat. Framers profit from binaries; regions pay.
lessonContent:
Unadvertised middles exist in most fights.
Paychecks plus habitat beat either-or.
Framers profit; regions pay for binaries.
Selective harvests sustain both sides.
Share this: fund one middle path.

title: The Honest Fork
question: When is a presented either-or actually legitimate rather than a false dilemma? Logicians apply exactly one test.
correctExplanation: Proven exhaustive and exclusive options — the disjuncts must cover all cases with no overlap. Forks earn legitimacy by proof.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is proven exhaustive, exclusive options. Volume, brevity, and pedigree miss it: legitimacy needs demonstrated coverage plus mutual exclusion. Test forks before walking them.
lessonContent:
Coverage plus exclusion legitimize forks.
Proof, not volume, validates dilemmas.
Test disjuncts before walking them.
Honest forks are rare and precious.
Share this: test one fork today.
